pending_qa.q: How much exercise is needed to reduce the risk of cancer through myokine release?
pending_qa.r: Just 30 minutes a day of aerobic physical activity can downregulate 13 types of cancers, with the most prominent being breast cancer, colon cancer, and prostate cancer. The mechanism involves a robust release of natural killer cells into the bloodstream, which travel to tumour sites and kill tumour cells. Anti-inflammatory effects from both resistance training and aerobic training also contribute to the anti-cancer benefits.

pending_qa.q: What is the danger of being 'active sedentary' and how does prolonged sitting affect health even if you exercise?
pending_qa.r: A major finding in 2025 from the Cleveland Clinic identified the danger of being 'active sedentary,' defined as people who exercise for 30 to 60 minutes but sit for the remaining 10 hours a day. If you sit for more than 10 hours a day, your risk of cardiovascular disease increases even if you meet weekly exercise goals, because prolonged sitting shuts down lipoprotein lipase, an enzyme essential for burning fat and cleaning glucose from the blood. Doing 10 air squats every hour for eight hours can compensate for a sedentary lifestyle, and this can outweigh the benefits of a 30-minute power walk.

pending_qa.q: What is the Norwegian 4x4 protocol and why is it considered the gold standard for improving VO2 max?
pending_qa.r: The Norwegian 4x4 involves getting your heart rate elevated to 90 to 95% of maximum for four minutes on, four minutes off, repeated four times. VO2 max, along with strength, is described as the strongest predictor of all-cause mortality, and it starts to decline from around age 35. Doing 20 minutes of VO2 max training per week is recommended just to maintain VO2 max levels.

pending_qa.q: What did Dr. Ben Levine's landmark study show about reversing the aging of the heart through exercise?
pending_qa.r: Dr. Ben Levine, a sports cardiologist, took a group of sedentary males with an average age of around 50 and subjected them to approximately four hours of exercise per week for two years, including one resistance training session, one high-intensity session at around 90% of maximum heart rate, and longer moderate sessions. At the end of two years, he found he had remodelled their hearts by 20 years, essentially turning 50-year-old hearts into 30-year-old hearts through physical activity alone. The heart retains its plasticity to be remodelled until the age of 65, after which it becomes too stiff for this reversal.

pending_qa.q: How does high blood pressure damage the brain and what blood pressure level should be maintained to protect cognitive function?
pending_qa.r: The brain is the most vascular-rich organ in the body, and hypertension — elevated blood pressure above 135 systolic — starts to kill off the capillaries, which are one cell thick and supply the blood-brain barrier and the outer cortex of the brain with blood. This leads to a breakdown of the blood-brain barrier, described as 'leaky brain,' allowing passive diffusion of harmful molecules into the brain. The SPRINT trial established the gold standard recommendation of 120 over 80, showing that aggressively managing blood pressure pharmacologically with ACE inhibitors preserved brain gray matter and cognitive functions in patients.

pending_qa.q: What role does a ketogenic diet play in managing Alzheimer's disease and why does the brain lose the ability to use glucose?
pending_qa.r: During Alzheimer's disease, the brain undergoes a metabolic crisis where it loses the ability to use glucose as its primary fuel source. In response, astrocytes begin breaking down the myelin sheath and produce ketone bodies as an alternative energy source for brain cells. A ketone-rich diet or exogenous ketones are recommended to support the brain during this crisis, alongside aggressive exercise and high omega-3 fatty acid intake.

pending_qa.q: Is Alzheimer's disease the leading cause of death for women and how does it ultimately kill patients?
pending_qa.r: Dementia is the number one killer of women in the UK and the number one cause of death in Australia for both men and women. Patients do not die of Alzheimer's disease specifically; instead, the brain progressively loses signals for basic functions, and patients can die of asphyxiation, loss of the ability to swallow, or falls due to lost balance. Once diagnosed, there is no cure and no reversal, making prevention during the preceding 20-year window critical.

pending_qa.q: What intensity of weight lifting is required to produce neural and brain benefits from resistance training?
pending_qa.r: All studies show that in order to produce the neural effects of resistance training, you need to be lifting at around 80% of your one repetition max (one RM). While hypertrophy — increase in muscle mass — can be achieved by lifting light with high reps or heavy with low reps, the brain-specific benefits require heavy lifting because it takes more neural real estate in the motor cortex and generates a greater neural drive. The heavier the lift, the greater the neural drive and the better the outcome for the brain.

pending_qa.q: If you could only do one exercise for the rest of your life to protect your brain, what should it be and why?
pending_qa.r: The deadlift is identified as the single best exercise for brain protection because, when done correctly, it uses almost every muscle in the body including the erector spinae, glutes, quads, serratus anterior, and calf muscles. The compounding nature of the movement — engaging nearly the full musculature — makes it comparable to a barbell squat as the most comprehensive single exercise. The greater the muscle recruitment, the greater the myokine release and neural drive beneficial to the brain.
